Important Note About the R Client

We maintain the R client to support our R user community, recognizing R as a foundational language in many data workflows. synapser is built on top of the Synapse Python client via the reticulate package. This lets us solve complex engineering problems, such as file transfers and caching, once in Python and reuse those solutions in R.

We recommend upgrading to version 3.0 or later of the Synapse R client. Starting with 3.0, the R client uses reticulate to manage its Python dependencies, which should make installation and updates easier. You do not need to set up Python yourself: reticulate installs a compatible Python and the Synapse Python client the first time synapser is loaded.

If you run into problems, see the Troubleshooting guide or open an issue. New features usually appear in the Python client first, so if you need one that synapser does not have yet, you can use the Python client directly. If you continue to run into environment or package version issues, you can also use the Synapse Python client via reticulate. See the Using synapseclient with R through reticulate.

We appreciate your patience and continued feedback as we work to improve the user experience across both clients.

synapser

Introducing synapser 3.0.0

synapser 3.0.0 is a major release built on version 4.15 of the Synapse Python client. It introduces object-oriented models: create an instance of a Synapse object, such as File(path = “data.csv”, parent_id = “syn123”), then pipe it into verb functions like synStore() and synGet(). It also brings:

  • No Python setup. When synapser is loaded, reticulate installs a compatible Python and the Synapse Python client for you. Python versions 3.11 to 3.15 are supported.
  • Current R dependencies. synapser works with current versions of reticulate (1.44.0 or later) and rjson, and requires R 4.2.0 or later.

This release is not backward compatible. Functions from earlier versions, such as synGetChildren() and synGetAnnotations(), have been removed. Before upgrading, see Key differences from the legacy API for how earlier calls map to the new API, and Supported Models and Functions for what this release supports.

Introduction

The synapser package provides an interface to Synapse, a collaborative workspace for reproducible data-intensive research projects, providing support for:

  • integrated presentation of data, code, and text
  • fine-grained access control
  • provenance tracking

The synapser package lets you communicate with the Synapse platform to create collaborative data analysis projects and access data using the R programming language. Other Synapse clients exist for Python, Java, and the web browser.

Supported Models and Functions

synapser 3.0.0 supports the following Synapse models. Each model’s reference page also lists the functions that work on it, such as synGetAcl(), synSetPermissions(), or synSyncFromSynapse().

Area Models
Projects, folders, and files Project, Folder, File, Link
Tables and views Table, Column, JsonSubColumn, VirtualTable, EntityView, MaterializedView, SubmissionView, Dataset, DatasetCollection, EntityRef
Provenance Activity, UsedEntity, UsedURL
Wikis WikiPage, WikiHeader, WikiHistorySnapshot, WikiOrderHint
Challenges and evaluations Evaluation, Submission, SubmissionStatus, SubmissionBundle
Users, teams, and organizations Team, UserProfile, UserPreference, Organization, JSONSchema
Storage StorageLocation, StorageLocationType
AI agents Agent, AgentSession, AgentPrompt

These functions work across models:

Task Functions
Connecting to Synapse synLogin, synLogout, synSetEndpoints
Getting, storing, and deleting entities synGet, synStore, synDelete, synSetProperties
Options for getting and storing FileOptions, ActivityOptions, TableOptions, LinkOptions, StoreFileOptions, StoreContainerOptions, StoreTableOptions, StoreJSONSchemaOptions, StoreGridOptions
Querying tables and views synQuery, synQueryPartMask
Download list (cart) synDownloadListAdd, synDownloadListRemove, synDownloadListClear, synDownloadListManifest, synDownloadListFiles, DownloadListItem
Utilities synFindEntityId, synIsSynapseId, synOnweb, synPrintEntity, synMd5Query, synSendMessage
REST API synRestGet, synRestPost, synRestPut, synRestDelete

See the reference index for the full list.

Requirements

  • R version 4.2.0 or higher (tested up to R 4.6.1)
  • reticulate 1.44.0 or higher
  • Synapse account

Note: You do not need to install Python yourself. When synapser is loaded, it declares its Python requirement via reticulate::py_require(), and reticulate downloads a compatible Python and the Synapse Python client into a managed environment on first use.

Installation

synapser 3.0.0 is distributed through R-universe, which provides ready-built binaries for Windows and macOS (Apple silicon and Intel). Install it with:

install.packages(
  "synapser",
  repos = c("https://sage-bionetworks.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org")
)

Listing CRAN alongside R-universe lets R pull synapser’s dependencies (such as reticulate and rjson) from CRAN.

Linux: R installs packages from source on Linux, and several of synapser’s dependencies contain compiled code. Install a C/C++ compiler and the libpng headers first, then run the command above:

# Ubuntu / Debian
sudo apt-get install -y build-essential libpng-dev
# Amazon Linux / RHEL / CentOS
sudo dnf install -y gcc gcc-c++ make libpng-devel

Then restart R and verify the installation:

library(synapser)
packageVersion("synapser")  # should be 3.0.0

The first library(synapser) may take a minute while reticulate downloads Python and the Synapse Python client. Later loads reuse the cached environment.

See the install guide for upgrading from synapser 2.x, installing an older version (2.x releases remain on RAN), installing from GitHub, and how synapser finds Python. If installation fails, see the Troubleshooting guide.

Usage

To get started, try logging in to Synapse. If you don’t already have a Synapse account, register here:

library(synapser)
synLogin()

To learn more about using synapser, visit the docs site or browse the package vignettes:

browseVignettes(package = "synapser")
